title: QBR: Inference Commander cadence & budget sync
summary: Quarterly check-in to align on usage trends, unexpected cost drivers from a recent campaign, latency incidents during peak, and next steps for a 6-week pilot on Dedicated capacity. Security questions surfaced around KMS and audit logs; Redwood to share SOC2 and pilot pricing. Agreed to run a short performance benchmark and cost projection within one week.
topics: Recent 2x usage spike and cost drivers
Latency incidents during peak traffic (04:00 UTC window)
Rollout cadence and success metrics for next quarter
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-30 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Tara Singh, Ethan Morales, Lina Park, Marcus Yeo (BrightCanvas)

Summary (auto): QBR-ish health check, focus on cost anomaly during marketing campaign, discussion about Dedicated pilot and security assurances; next steps: pilot pricing, SOC2, benchmark run.

[00:00] Morgan Chen: alright everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off — I see the calendar says 52 minutes so we'll try to keep to that. quick roll call?
[00:12] Tara Singh: Tara here — head of ML at BrightCanvas.
[00:15] Ethan Morales: Ethan, VP engineering.
[00:18] Lina Park: Lina, handling FinOps.
[00:20] Marcus Yeo: Marcus from security.
[00:22] Morgan Chen: great thanks. Diego and Priya with me from Redwood. Diego is our solutions engineer, Priya is your CSM.
[00:29] Diego Alvarez: hi!
[00:31] Priya Kapoor: hi all.
[00:33] Morgan Chen: first item — usage spike. Lina you flagged a 2x token usage on July 18 campaign — can you talk through what you saw?
[00:45] Lina Park: yeah so we ran a promotion and traffic spiked, um the tokens jumped more than we'd forecasted. at first we thought it was prompt length but it's actually a combination: more concurrent chats and some longer context windows coming from an A/B test. cost went up sharply, it's showing on last bill.
[01:02] Ethan Morales: right, we also changed the rerank frequency in the app which increased per-request tokens.
[01:08] Morgan Chen: got it. Diego — any telemetry that helps pinpoint whether tokens or model choice was the main driver?
[01:15] Diego Alvarez: from the traces we pulled, most of the extra cost came from longer avg token per session — the model stayed the same. also there was less effective prefix caching because session ids weren't reused in the test — so KV cash, sorry KV cache didn't hit as often. that amplifies cost.
[01:36] Tara Singh: yeah we noticed the cache keys were being regenerated by the experiment.
[01:39] Morgan Chen: ok that's useful. on the latency side Lina mentioned a couple of incidents around 04:00 UTC — Marcus, can you describe the impact?
[01:48] Marcus Yeo: small but visible spikes in p99 latency, users saw some timeouts in step flows. it correlated with the campaign peak and a backend batch hitting the same model route.
[02:00] Diego Alvarez: we saw a queue buildup on some of the shared host nodes; it looks like request routing skewed because auto-scale didn't spin up additional capacity fast enough for that traffic shape.
[02:10] Priya Kapoor: this is where Dedicated pulse helps — you get predictable throughput and we can configure burst capacity to cover those marketing peaks.
[02:20] Ethan Morales: question — how big a delta in cost do you expect for Dedicated? we need to present to finance.
[02:26] Morgan Chen: good question. high-level: Dedicated moves you to reserved GPU pools (monthly commit) so your per-token unit cost goes down but you pay commit. for a 6-week pilot we can model a blended cost showing break-even vs hosted. we'll send a pilot pricing sheet.
[02:40] Lina Park: do you have an example model? like for our traffic profile — 2M tokens/day peak — how do numbers shift?
[02:47] Diego Alvarez: we'll run a projection. quick aside — quantization and batching suggestions in Redwood Optimize could also reduce cost on host while you evaluate Dedicated; sometimes small config changes give 15-30% savings.
[03:02] Tara Singh: is there any quality tradeoff with quantization? we can't regress the assistant's output.
[03:08] Diego Alvarez: depends on model and quantization profile; we recommend running evals on your prompt set — Redwood Optimize can automate that and flag regressions.
[03:18] Ethan Morales: ok let's add that as a step.
[03:20] Morgan Chen: security — Marcus you had questions about KMS and audit logs?
[03:25] Marcus Yeo: yeah we want to know if customer-managed keys are supported in Dedicated and how audit logs are surfaced. also curious about SSO/SAML for console and token-level access controls.
[03:36] Priya Kapoor: Dedicated supports customer KMS integration and we surface audit logs via the console, plus you can push to your SIEM. SSO/SAML is supported — we'll share the security pack including SOC 2 and ISO notes.
[03:48] Marcus Yeo: ok we'll need the formal SOC2 report and specifics about rotation and HSM.
[03:54] Morgan Chen: we'll attach the SOC2 link and a short security appendix for the pilot.
[03:58] Lina Park: timeline — we want to pilot in mid-August, run 6 weeks, and make a commit decision end of September. is that feasible?
[04:07] Diego Alvarez: yes that timeline is doable. we'll provision a Dedicated pool for the pilot and we can start with a smaller reserve.
[04:15] Ethan Morales: who will be the tech owners on the Redwood side during the pilot?
[04:19] Morgan Chen: Diego will support the benchmarks and day-to-day SE tasks; Priya will coordinate SLOs and billing; Morgan (me) will own commercial updates.
[04:29] Diego Alvarez: quick technical note — to minimize drift during the pilot we suggest pinning model versions and using canary rollouts for any architecture tweaks.
[04:37] Tara Singh: yes that helps. also, Diego, can you run a performance benchmark against our most common prompt set? we want p50/p95/p99 numbers for both hosted and Dedicated.
[04:47] Diego Alvarez: absolutely — we'll run against a sample set. can we get that prompt corpus exported?
[04:52] Tara Singh: I'll share a sanitized corpus by end of day Friday.
[04:55] Priya Kapoor: note: for benchmarks we may need temporary elevated quotas — we'll request that from infra.
[05:01] Morgan Chen: next, costs — Lina asked about an immediate mitigation while pilot is stood up. Diego you mentioned caching and batching. any quick wins we can deploy in 1–2 sprints?
[05:12] Diego Alvarez: yes — enable prefix/KV caching for session reuse, lower rerank frequency in non-critical paths, and set smarter batching windows in the runtime. most customers ship the caching change and see immediate token reduction.
[05:25] Lina Park: how intrusive are those changes? dev effort?
[05:28] Diego Alvarez: low to medium — mostly configuration and a small change to how session keys are generated. we can provide a remediation playbook.
[05:36] Marcus Yeo: on the compliance side, what's the data retention behavior for log storage during pilot? we need to ensure PII isn't retained.
[05:44] Priya Kapoor: you control retention window for logs and we can set anonymization. we'll include retention defaults and options in the security appendix.
[05:52] Ethan Morales: great. one more commercial point — can you give an example of SLA for Dedicated? uptime, latency targets?
[05:58] Morgan Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; exact numbers vary by commitment level. for the pilot we'll propose a guarded SLA and runbook for incident response.
[06:10] Tara Singh: ok. let's talk about success metrics for the pilot — what should we measure to decide to expand?
[06:17] Morgan Chen: recommend metrics: 1) per-token cost delta vs baseline; 2) p99 latency improvement; 3) percent of requests served from cache; 4) operational stability (incidents/week); 5) business metric lift (engagement).
[06:33] Lina Park: finance will want a cost projection so include blended and worst-case scenarios.
[06:38] Priya Kapoor: noted — we'll include a 3-scenario cost model.
[06:41] Diego Alvarez: small point — watch for model variant fallbacks. if a variant is quantized we should test for quality regression in your eval suite.
[06:50] Marcus Yeo: security will also want to run an onboarding checklist before we go live with pilot traffic.
[06:55] Morgan Chen: agreed.
[06:57] Tara Singh: quick question — anyone else mentioned as competitor when we talk to finance? they asked about Anthropic and Google Vertex.
[07:04] Morgan Chen: yes we hear that often. Redwood's differentiator here is the production-first runtime and the routing/caching controls that reduce unit economics.
[07:13] Ethan Morales: ok let's wrap with explicit next steps.
[07:17] Morgan Chen: priya, can you read back?
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: sure — action items: 1) Morgan to send pilot pricing and 3-scenario cost model (due 2028-08-02). 2) Diego to run performance benchmark against Tara's corpus (start when corpus received; results by 2028-08-06). 3) Priya to share SOC2 and security appendix (due 2028-08-01). 4) Tara to share sanitized prompt corpus (by 2028-08-03). 5) Lina/Ethan to review internal approval and confirm pilot commit budget (decision by 2028-08-10).
[07:48] Tara Singh: that looks right.
[07:50] Morgan Chen: anything else?
[07:52] Ethan Morales: one small ask — can we get a short spreadsheet that shows expected monthly run rate for Dedicated at different reserves?
[07:59] Morgan Chen: yes we'll include that in the pilot pricing doc.
[08:03] Priya Kapoor: I'll schedule a technical kickoff the week of Aug 6th after benchmarks.
[08:09] Morgan Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in writing.
[08:13] Meeting end.
